chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him (peace be upon him) about the locust, if we find it dead in the desert or in the water, is it permissible to eat? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not eat it.'

He (the narrator) said, 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about the Dabba (young locust) from the locusts, is it permissible to eat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until it is capable of flying.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating dead or young locusts in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the conditions for the permissibility of consuming locusts, distinguishing between those found dead and immature nymphs. It establishes that locusts must be alive and capable of flight to be considered Halal, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that insects are generally permissible only if they are alive and not found dead in their natural habitat.
